cards.text: Meet Paul and Barnabas, two men carrying the good news about Jesus from town to town. They just got driven out of Pisidian Antioch and shook the dust off their feet on the way out (Acts 13:50-51). Now they're in Iconium, and as usual, first stop: the Jewish synagogue.

cards.question: In the synagogue at Iconium, Paul and Barnabas speak so well that something big happens. What is it?

answers.text: A great number of Jews and Greeks believe
The leaders ask them to preach every Sabbath
The rulers invite them to speak at the palace

cards.text: But the unbelieving Jews stir up the Gentiles and poison their minds against the brothers. Somebody ALWAYS has to be the comment section.

cards.question: With minds in Iconium getting poisoned against them, Paul and Barnabas leave town right away.
Paul and Barnabas keep speaking boldly for the Lord in Iconium. How does the Lord back up the message of His grace?

answers.text: He enables them to perform signs and wonders
He sends an angel to stand guard beside them
He makes the city rulers protect them

cards.text: Now the city is divided, some siding with the Jews and some with the apostles. It's a family group chat after somebody touched the thermostat.
Then it turns ugly. The Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat Paul and Barnabas and stone them.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas find out about the plan to stone them in Iconium. What do they do?
Once they reach Lystra and Derbe, Paul and Barnabas lie low and stop preaching for a while.

cards.text: In Lystra there's a man sitting, crippled in his feet. He's been lame from birth and has never walked.

cards.question: The man in Lystra is listening to Paul. Paul looks intently at him and sees that he has ___ to be healed.
In a loud voice, Paul calls out to the man who has never walked, "Stand up on your feet!" What does the man do?

answers.text: He jumps up and begins to walk
He stands but cannot take a step
He asks Paul to pray for him first

cards.text: The crowds in Lystra just watched a man who never walked JUMP to his feet. They lift up their voices in the Lycaonian language: "The gods have come down to us in human form!"
Friend, I've been hopping around on this gold base for years, and that man outjumped me on his very first try.

cards.question: The crowd in Lystra decides Paul and Barnabas are gods. What do they call Barnabas?
The crowd calls Paul Hermes, because he is the chief ___.

cards.text: The priest of Zeus, whose temple is just outside the city, brings bulls and wreaths to the city gates. Friend, that is a LOT of planning for a misunderstanding.

cards.question: What is the priest of Zeus hoping to do with the bulls and wreaths at the city gates?

answers.text: Offer a sacrifice along with the crowds
Crown Paul and Barnabas as kings
Lead a parade through the whole city

cards.question: When Barnabas and Paul find out about the sacrifice, they tear their clothes and rush into the crowd.

cards.text: They shout, "Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you." Meanwhile, somebody compliments ONE of my cookies and I start signing autographs.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas tell the crowd to turn from these ___ things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.

cards.text: Then they tell the crowd that in past generations, God let all nations go their own way.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas say God has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness. What do they point to?

answers.text: Rain from heaven and fruitful seasons
Stars that light up the night sky

cards.question: Once Paul and Barnabas finish speaking, the crowds in Lystra calm down easily.

cards.text: Then some Jews arrive from Antioch and Iconium and win over the same crowds that wanted to sacrifice to Paul and Barnabas. Friend, that's a U-turn with NO blinker.

cards.question: The crowds in Lystra have been won over against Paul. What do they do to him?

answers.text: Stone him and drag him outside the city
Throw him into the city prison
Send him back to Iconium in chains

cards.question: When the crowd drags Paul outside the city, they think he is dead.
The disciples gather around Paul outside the city. What does Paul do?

answers.text: Gets up and goes back into the city
Asks them to carry him to Derbe
Rests outside the city for a week

cards.text: He walks right back into the city that just stoned him, and the next day he leaves with Barnabas for Derbe. I bump my chef's hat on the oven door and need to lie down for an hour.
Paul and Barnabas make it to Derbe and preach the gospel to that city.

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas preach the gospel in Derbe. How does it go?
After Derbe, Paul and Barnabas steer clear of Lystra and Iconium on the way home.

cards.text: They go right back to Lystra, Iconium and Antioch, the same places they had to escape. I once dropped a tray by the third oven and walked the long way around it for a MONTH.

cards.question: Back in Lystra, Iconium and Antioch, what do Paul and Barnabas do for the disciples?

answers.text: Strengthen them and urge them to keep the faith
Collect money for the church in Jerusalem
Tell them to move somewhere much safer

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas tell the disciples, "We must endure many ___ to enter the kingdom of God."
Before moving on, Paul and Barnabas set something up in each church. What do they do?
As they appoint elders in each church, Paul and Barnabas pray and fast.

cards.text: After passing through Pisidia, they come to Pamphylia and speak the word in Perga. That's the same Perga where John left them to go back to Jerusalem (Acts 13:13).

cards.question: After speaking the word in Perga, Paul and Barnabas go down to ___.

cards.text: From Attalia they sail to Antioch, where this whole journey started, and where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work they had just completed (Acts 13:1-3). Full circle, friend.

cards.question: Back in Antioch, Paul and Barnabas gather the church together. What do they do?

answers.text: Report all that God had done through them
Ask the church to send a bigger team
Choose who goes on the next trip

cards.question: Paul and Barnabas tell the church in Antioch how God opened the door of ___ to the Gentiles.

cards.text: And they spend a long time there with the disciples. After getting stoned, chased out of town and nearly sacrificed to, friend, I'd stay a LONG time too.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 6 quotes "We must endure many ___ to enter the kingdom of God.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke "Somebody ALWAYS has to be the comment section" points at the unbelieving Jews themselves rather than at their human situation. It can read as a jab at a specific ethnic and religious group named in the text. Swap it for self-deprecating humor, or for a joke that looks at the moment with respect.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke ("that man outjumped me on his very first try"). It tells no part of the passage. It also cites Acts 14:11 while it jokes about the jump in Acts 14:10. Fold the joke into a story card that carries a beat of the passage, or cut it.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "healer" is arguably true in this passage, since Paul is the one who healed the lame man (Acts 14:10). A baker could argue that Paul is the chief healer. Replace it with a word that is clearly false for Paul everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Acts 14:19 says some Jews arrived and won over the crowds, then "They stoned Paul." The text leaves open exactly who "they" are. Card 14 ("The crowds in Lystra... What do they do to him?") and card 15 ("When the crowd drags Paul") pin the stoning on the crowds alone. Reword both cards so they keep "they" open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: John appears here for the first time in the walkthrough ("the same Perga where John left them"), but the card never says who he is. Acts 13:5 calls him their helper. Add a simple identification, like "John, their helper."

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."
